followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors from the documentation:

1. **Task type match.** The request blends two things — a customer-service complaint response (Support Dialogue) and producing a well-formed formal letter (Creative Generation / open-ended composition). Both of those are areas where Curlew has clear, meaningful advantages on the internal evals.

2. **Eval gaps that exceed the noise threshold.** The documentation says differences under 2.0 points are just run-to-run variance. Here the gaps are well past that:
   - Support Dialogue: Curlew 85.7 vs. Whimbrel 79.4 (~6.3)
   - Creative Generation: Curlew 87.2 vs. Whimbrel 78.8 (~8.4)
   
   So this isn't a coin flip — Curlew is genuinely stronger on the dimensions that matter for this query.

3. **Stated preferences pointing the same way.** Curlew self-reports liking open-ended generative work (74) and warm, collaborative exchanges (63). A courteous letter resolving a complaint fits that profile. The docs caution that preferences don't affect output quality, so I treated this as a minor tiebreaker rather than the main reason — but it lined up with the eval-based decision rather than cutting against it.

The capability evals did the real work; the preference data just confirmed there was nothing pulling the other direction. The "don't mess it up this time" framing also signals the user cares about quality, which reinforced picking the stronger model on these dimensions.
